paragraphs.text: Prophesy again against him, for my people’s greater comfort. The Jews - noted ever to have been a light, serial, and fanatical nation, apt to work themselves into the fool’s paradise of a sublime dotage - expounding this prophecy according to the letter, conclude that Christ is not yet come, because these things here foretold are not yet fulfilled. When he doth come, they say, he shall set up his kingdom at Jerusalem, gather all Israel out of all coasts unto himself there, send each one to his own tribe, and that most certainly, by the operation of his Holy Spirit. There they shall be no sooner settled, and the kingdom not yet fully established, but Gog and Magog shall bring a huge army against Jerusalem, where they shall fall by the sword, lie unburied, &c.
paragraphs.anchor: Prophesy against Gog.

paragraphs.text: Convertam vel conteram te. {a} See Eze 38:3.
paragraphs.anchor: And I will turn thee back.

paragraphs.text: Or, Strike thee with six plagues, or draw thee back with a hook of six teeth. {as Eze 38:4} Sextabo re.
paragraphs.anchor: And leave but the sixth part of thee.

paragraphs.text: This is much and often inculcated, that it is God who brings in and drives out the Church’s enemies. This is a quieting consideration.
paragraphs.anchor: And will cause thee to come.

paragraphs.text: {a} In frusta vel scintillas redigam te. - Pintus.

I will disarm thee. As Herodotus {a} reporteth of Sennacherib and his Assyrians in Egypt, that their quivers, bow strings, and targets were gnawn to pieces by mice and rats in one night, so that they were forced to flee for their lives. And as our chroniclers {b} tell us, that in the battle between Edward III of England and Philip of France, there fell such a piercing shower of rain as dissolved their strings, and made their bows unuseful.
paragraphs.anchor: And I will smite thy bow out of thy left hand.

paragraphs.text: {a} Lib. ii.
Thither thou shalt come indeed, as Antiochus did into the temple, antichrist into the Church of God, {2Th 2:4} but there thou shalt take thy end.
paragraphs.anchor: Thou shalt fall upon, the mountains of Israel.

paragraphs.text: Heb., The face of the field, which thou shall dung with thy dead carcase.
paragraphs.anchor: Thou shall fall upon the open field.

paragraphs.text: So God will one day on Rome, that Radix omnium malorum root of all evil things. {Rev 18:18-19}
paragraphs.anchor: And I will send a fire on Magog.

paragraphs.text: Who must not think there to moat up themselves against my fire.
paragraphs.anchor: And among them that dwell carelessly in the isles.

paragraphs.text: As if I were less able to deliver my people, or less mindful of my promises.
paragraphs.anchor: I will not let them pollute my holy name.

paragraphs.text: It is as good as done. So, "Babylon is fallen" - i.e., It will fall certainly, quickly, utterly.
paragraphs.anchor: Behold, it is come, and it is done.

paragraphs.text: O dieculam illam! O that short time. When shall it once be? O mora! Christe veni. O delay! Christ, come.
paragraphs.anchor: This is the day.

paragraphs.text: Hyperbolical expressions; though the Jews hold otherwise. See on Eze 39:1.
paragraphs.anchor: And they that dwell.

paragraphs.text: Do not the Church’s champions so at this day, ever since they proclaimed and proved the Pope to be that antichrist; burning up his weapons - his false doctrines and heresies - by the fire of God’s Word, and giving their bodies to be burned for the testimony of Jesus?
paragraphs.anchor: Shall set on fire and burn the weapons.

paragraphs.text: i.e., Diutissime et saepissime! Most long and most often. This seven years is not yet out. The Jesuits say Satan sent Luther, and God sent them to withstand him. But there is a succession of Luthers to find them work enough still, and to burn up their weapons that the churches may be at rest.
paragraphs.anchor: And they shall burn them with fire seven years

paragraphs.text: This must needs be hyperbolic, as are also sundry other passages in Holy Scripture. When Luther burnt the Pope’s decrees and decretals at Wittemberg, it was a fair fire doubtless, as Solon once said of the fire he caused to be made at Athens of the bills and bonds of the Athenian usurers.
paragraphs.anchor: So that they shall take no wood.

paragraphs.text: That is all the portion or possession he gets in the Holy Land.
paragraphs.anchor: I will give unto Gog a place there of graves.

paragraphs.text: The Dead Sea, or the lake of Sodom - a fit place for antichrist to be buried in: he shall at last be cast alive into a worse lake. {Rev 19:20}
paragraphs.anchor: On the east of the sea.

paragraphs.text: By reason of stench, or the mouths of passengers from speaking evil of God’s people.
paragraphs.anchor: And it shall stop the noses of passengers.

paragraphs.text: For a lasting monument of God’s great mercy, in ridding the country of such pests.
paragraphs.anchor: And they shall call it.

paragraphs.text: That is, a long while; like as the Reformed Churches were in rooting out Popery, those damnable doctrines, ceremonies, images, relics, bulls, and books. Here in England, the Romish religion stood a whole month and more after the death of Queen Mary, as before. December 27, it was permitted that the Epistles, Gospels, Ten Commandments, Lord’s Prayer, Creed, and Litany should be used in the Vulgate tongue. March 22, when the Estates of the realm were assembled, by renewing of a law of Edward VI, was granted the whole use of the Lord’s Supper - that is, under both kinds. June 24, the sacrifice of the mass was abolished, and the liturgy in the English tongue established. In July, the oath of supremacy was ministered; and in August, images were removed out of churches, broken or burnt. {a}
paragraphs.anchor: And seven months shall the house of Israel be burying of them.

paragraphs.text: “ Tantae molis erat Romanam abscondere gentem. ”
{a} Camden’s Elisabeth.

A monument or trophy of their triumph. When the Switzers, A.D. 1443, had vanquished the Thuricenses in battle, they banqueted in the place where they won the victory, using the dead bodies of their adversaries instead of stools and tables. {a}
paragraphs.anchor: And it shall be to them a renown.

paragraphs.text: {a} Lanquet Chron., p. 263.

Viros quotidianos; men that shall stick to it, making it their business: Pollinctores: vespillones. So do our public professors and others, to confute Popish tenets, and to decry their customs. In doing whereof, they are assidui et accubui. constant and near.
paragraphs.anchor: And they shall sever out men of continual employment.

paragraphs.text: A statue, pillar, or sepulchral monument, that the butlers may bury it. Oh that in like sort God would cause the prophet, all relics and rags of Popery, and other heresy, together with the unclean spirit, to pass out of our land. {Zec 13:2}
paragraphs.anchor: Then shall he set up a sign by it.

paragraphs.text: i.e., Multitude or tumult; and all to keep up the memory of that signal victory. Near unto the University of Cambridge, on the southeast side, there appear aloft certain high hills called Gog Magog hills; but wherefore I know not. But not far from them is Heretics’ hill, so called by the Papists because Bilney and Latimer were wont there to walk.
paragraphs.anchor: And also the name of the city shall be Hamonah

paragraphs.text: A further explanation of that which had been said. {Eze 39:4}
paragraphs.anchor: Speak unto every feathered fowl.
Assemble yourselves.

paragraphs.text: To this great slaughter of enemies whom I do sacrifice, as it were, to my justice.
paragraphs.anchor: To my sacrifice.

paragraphs.text: Whose flesh may he, perhaps, more delicate.
paragraphs.anchor: Ye shall eat the flesh of the mighty.

paragraphs.text: Blood royal, of a noble alloy. Sed nihil inde colligas, quam perpetuam eorum damnationem qui verbum Dei persequuntur, quique populum Israel spiritualem exagitant. {a} It importeth the eternal damnation of atheists and antichrists.
paragraphs.anchor: And drink the blood.

paragraphs.text: {a} Oecolampadius.
Or, Of my good cheer. So God calleth it, to show how well pleased he is with the destruction of his Church’s enemies.
paragraphs.anchor: Of my sacrifice.

paragraphs.text: i.e., With men that ride on horses, and fight out of chariots.
paragraphs.anchor: With horses and chariots

paragraphs.text: Antiochus did so, and Maximinus the emperor, and other tyrants, when seized upon by such judgments of God as they could neither avoid nor abide.
paragraphs.anchor: And all the heathen shall see my judgment.

paragraphs.text: Their experience shall breed confidence.
paragraphs.anchor: From that day and forward.

paragraphs.text: They shall be convinced of the equability of my proceedings, and the truth of my menaces.
paragraphs.anchor: And the heathen shall know.

paragraphs.text: I have not shown my sovereignty, or exercised tyranny towards them, but done them right.
paragraphs.anchor: According to their uncleanness.

paragraphs.text: Three things he here promiseth his people, notwithstanding all the sorrow, (1.) Effectual vocation; (2.) Justification here; (3.) Glorification. {Eze 39:29} The Sun of righteousness loves not to set in a cloud.
paragraphs.anchor: Now will I bring again.

paragraphs.text: Or, Zealous; "the zeal of the Lord of hosts," his free grace, "shall effect it,"
paragraphs.anchor: And will be jealous.

paragraphs.text: Are become soundly ashamed of their sinful practices: Hoc enim ingenium est verae fidei, saith Oecolampadius, for this is the nature of true faith, to blush and bleed for sins past.
paragraphs.anchor: After that they have borne their shame.

paragraphs.text: And so settled on their lease through carnal security.
paragraphs.anchor: When they dwelt safely in their land.

paragraphs.text: i.e., Have fully shown my sanctity and majesty, both by their punishment and by their deliverance.
paragraphs.anchor: And am sanctified in them

paragraphs.text: Here the Jews triumph and say, When was this promise ever fulfilled? and how, then, can the Messiah be come already? Hereunto it is rightly answered, that this prophecy is to be taken partly literally, and so it was fulfilled at the return of the captives out of Babylon. See Ezr 3:1. Partly spiritually; and so Christ will at the last day raise up every one of his elect, - that Israel indeed, - and gather them to himself; not one of them shall be missing. {a}
paragraphs.anchor: And have left none of them any more there.

paragraphs.text: {a} Lavat. in loc.
They shall have beatiful vision and fruition for ever. See on Eze 39:25.
paragraphs.anchor: Neither Will I hide my face any more from them.

paragraphs.text: Have already, and will do yet more liberally in the days of the gospel. {Act 2:2-7 Joh 7:38}
paragraphs.anchor: For I have poured out my spirit.
